summary: Somalia requires every foreign visitor to hold an electronic authorisation (E-Visa/ETAS) obtained at etas.gov.so before departure — the Immigration and Citizenship Agency launched it on 1 September 2025 in place of applying on arrival. The self-declared Republic of Somaliland runs its own, entirely separate entry regime.

Immigration and Citizenship Agency of Somalia — launch of the Electronic Travel Authorisation System (E-Visa/ETAS)

passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Somalia.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: Not an entry requirement: WHO's country list and CDC both state Somalia does not require proof of yellow fever vaccination. WHO and CDC generally do not recommend the vaccine, except that it may be considered for the southern regions (Bakool, Banaadir, Bay, Galguduud, Gedo, Hiiraan, Lower and Middle Juba, Lower and Middle Shabelle). Check the rules of any country you travel on to afterwards.

source.name: WHO — International Travel and Health: country list of vaccination requirements (2022, revised 2023)

vaccinations.name: Malaria prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: Malaria is present throughout Somalia all year, with risk lower and seasonal in the north and higher in the centre and south, including Mogadishu. Antimalarial tablets, repellent and bed nets are recommended — talk to a travel clinic before your trip.

source.name: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — Travelers' health: Somalia

travelInsurance.text: No official Somali source states an insurance requirement. Many standard travel policies exclude countries under do-not-travel advice, so check that your cover includes Somalia and medical evacuation.

source.name: Immigration and Citizenship Agency of Somalia — launch of the Electronic Travel Authorisation System (E-Visa/ETAS)

onwardTicket.text: No official source states a return-ticket requirement. The eTAS application form asks you to upload a flight booking and a sponsor letter, and the FCDO says you may need a letter of invitation on arrival.

source.name: Immigration and Citizenship Agency of Somalia — launch of the Electronic Travel Authorisation System (E-Visa/ETAS)

proofOfFunds.text: No official source states a proof-of-funds requirement or amount. The eTAS application asks for a sponsor organisation and host details instead.

source.name: Immigration and Citizenship Agency of Somalia — launch of the Electronic Travel Authorisation System (E-Visa/ETAS)

currencyLimits.text: In Somaliland, cash or travellers cheques worth USD 10,000 or more must be declared. No official threshold is published for the rest of Somalia.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Somalia travel advice: entry requirements

notes: Alcohol is illegal in Somalia and may not be brought into the country.
Narcotics are strictly prohibited; khat is legal and widely traded domestically.

payments.text: Somalia runs on US dollar cash and mobile money — services such as EVC Plus dominate daily payments, and shilling notes are used mainly for small change. Card acceptance is rare outside a handful of Mogadishu hotels; bring clean, recent USD notes.

safety.text: Virtually every government advises against all travel to Somalia due to terrorism, armed conflict, crime and a very high kidnapping risk. Al-Shabaab regularly attacks hotels, government sites and the airport road in Mogadishu, and visitors move with pre-arranged armed security. Somaliland is calmer: the UK advises against all but essential travel to its Awdal, Maroodijeh (Hargeisa) and Sahil regions, and against all travel to the rest of Somalia, including the rest of Somaliland.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Somalia travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: December to February — the Jilal dry season — is the coolest, driest window; the Gu rains fall roughly April to June, and the coast is hot and humid for much of the year.

tips.text: Somalia is under do-not-travel advisories from virtually every government — terrorism and kidnapping risks are severe, independent tourism is effectively impossible, and visitors travel with armed escorts arranged before arrival.

Somaliland runs its own entry regime — flights to Hargeisa require a separate Somaliland visa (issued on arrival or through its missions for many nationalities), and federal Somali visas are not accepted there, nor Somaliland visas in Mogadishu.

The E-Visa/ETAS has been mandatory for all foreign nationals since 1 September 2025 and is applied for before departure, not on arrival. Apply only at etas.gov.so, well ahead of travel, and keep a copy of your approval to show on arrival.
Bring clean, recent US dollar notes — cash dollars and mobile money pay for nearly everything, and ATMs accepting foreign cards are scarce and unreliable.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Somalia?
faq.answer: Yes — every foreign visitor needs one. Since 1 September 2025 Somalia's Immigration and Citizenship Agency requires all foreign nationals to apply for their E-Visa/ETAS online at etas.gov.so before the journey rather than on arrival. No official source publishes the fee; it is paid with the online application.

faq.question: Is it safe to travel to Somalia?
faq.answer: No — Somalia is one of the highest-risk destinations in the world. Governments advise against all travel due to terrorism, kidnapping and armed conflict, and the few visitors who go travel with professional security arranged in advance.

faq.question: Is Somaliland's visa different from Somalia's?
faq.answer: Yes. The self-declared Republic of Somaliland controls its own borders: travelers flying into Hargeisa need a Somaliland visa, and a Somali federal visa or eVisa is not valid there. The two entry systems are completely separate.

faq.question: Can I pay for the Somali visa on arrival in cash?
faq.answer: Not according to any official source. Since 1 September 2025 the Immigration and Citizenship Agency requires every foreign national to obtain the E-Visa/ETAS online before travelling, and the fee is paid with the online application. No official page publishes a visa-on-arrival fee.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Somalia?
faq.answer: No. WHO's country list and CDC both state Somalia does not require a yellow fever certificate for entry. You may still need one for the next country on your route if you have been in Somalia or another risk country, so check that country's rules.
